summary: Primary-source audit confirms that GJR 15.11 gives a decreasing net for arbitrary targets. Weak smoothness uses harmonic tropicalizations; Wanner's continuous-target theorem and Thuillier's all-domain lisse functions cannot supply the missing conclusions. All seven supplied source hashes match.
detailedSummary: The actual GJR PDF distinguishes its arbitrary-target net from the sequence constructed for an individual piecewise real-linear target. Its harmonic-coordinate definitions, pullbacks, finite Galois descent and scalar-extension integration formula were checked. GR supplies the arbitrary extended-real classical starting class, normalization, finite classical descent, interior-to-curve subharmonic extension and the maximum principle. Wanner's field, curve, residue and finite-continuous-target restrictions were retained. The saved CD v2 numbering and ordinary smooth stages were checked separately. The requested artifacts were produced; two final TeX passes succeeded, but these checks do not verify the new mathematical proofs.
text:
The published premises used below were checked against the seven supplied caches.

GR, arXiv:2506.13548v2, Definition 4.1 defines classical psh using every analytic extension field and every analytic curve, with upper semicontinuous values in R union {-infinity}. GR 3.4.1 identifies its class on a smooth connected strict curve over a nontrivially valued field with Thuillier subharmonic functions together with the constant minus infinity. Proposition 4.2 gives ordinary sheafiness, maxima, positive linear combinations, scalar stability, analytic pullback and descent along finite surjective morphisms. Proposition 3.5(3) permits an upper semicontinuous function subharmonic on a curve's analytic interior to extend as subharmonic to the whole curve. Theorem 6.1 gives the local maximum principle at analytic interior points. Theorem 6.5 permits a pointwise limit of a net of classical psh functions when the limit is upper semicontinuous. Lemma 3.9 and its proof give finite normalization of reduced strict curves, rig-smoothness over perfect fields, exceptional discrete rigid points, the quotient property and local separation into finitely many branches.

GJR, arXiv:2111.05741, works over a complete nontrivially valued field on good strictly analytic spaces. Definition 5.1 uses strict affinoid G-coverings. Definition 8.1 uses integer-PL harmonic coordinates for harmonic tropicalizations. Proposition 7.5 expresses real harmonic germs through finitely many integer harmonic germs; 7.6 and Remark 8.2(4) preserve these coordinates under morphisms and every analytic scalar extension. Definitions 10.3 and 10.7 define weakly smooth functions by smooth Lagerberg functions in harmonic tropicalizations, sheafified on ordinary open sets. Section 10.8 gives pullback and Proposition 10.9 gives joint-chart equality. Ordinary CLD forms are included by Remark 10.10, but the reverse inclusion is not asserted. Proposition 14.2 gives finite Galois descent. Proposition 14.5(1) gives equality of integrals under finite Galois scalar extension, WITHOUT a degree multiplier. Sections 11–12 justify integration and current differentiation on Hausdorff boundaryless pure-dimensional spaces.

The actual GJR PDF, pages 80–81, was rendered and visually inspected. Proposition 15.11 states: for a smooth curve, meaning rig-smooth and boundaryless, over a nontrivially valued field, an arbitrary Thuillier-subharmonic function admits a decreasing NET of weakly smooth psh functions on each relatively compact ordinary open subset. The proof's final sequence concerns a single piecewise real-linear target. It does not establish a sequence for the initial arbitrary target. The proof expressly allows arbitrary real subdivisions without claiming that they are formal-model skeletons. Proposition 15.9 concerns the indicated strict subgraphs and piecewise (Z,Gamma)-linear harmonic functions. Proposition 15.7 identifies real harmonic functions with Thuillier harmonic functions. Remark 15.10 explicitly allows harmonic functions that are weakly smooth and not ordinary CLD smooth.

Thuillier's thesis, tel-00010990v1, distinguishes the all-domain site X_G and strict rigid site X_R in 2.1.1. Its Definition 3.2.1 of lisse uses all-domain affinoid coverings. Theorem 3.4.2 constructs a decreasing family indexed by finite subsets. No strict GJR real-PL membership or sequence is inferred merely from that theorem.

Wanner, arXiv:1801.04713v3, assumes an algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued field. Corollary 5.4 assumes a smooth proper algebraic curve, a residue field algebraic over a finite field or the projective-line/Mumford alternatives, and a finite continuous current-psh target on an open subset. Its compact Dini argument depends on that continuity. These restrictions are not silently applied to the original arbitrary classical class.

The actual saved CD arXiv:1204.6277v2 uses Definition 8.1.1, Lemma 8.1.4, Proposition 8.1.5 and Proposition 8.3.1 for ordinary smooth positive generators, transfinite decreasing-sequence stages, pullbacks and current positivity. Corollary 15.1.2 describes ordinary analytic smooth charts. Lemmas 1.2.10–1.2.11 give the relevant Lagerberg positivity cones and linear pullbacks. These results do not put every classical function in the first ordinary smooth stage or identify ordinary smoothness with weak smoothness. The other GR cache concerns strict real-PL semipositivity and is not used to identify arbitrary lisse functions as weakly smooth. Berkovich 1993 Proposition 1.5.5 supplies boundary composition, as restated in GR 2.11. No unpublished book premise is used.

summary: Draft sequence theorem for arbitrary classical psh germs on reduced boundaryless good strict curves over complete perfect nontrivially valued fields with a countable dense subset, including multibranch singularities. Normalization approximants are aligned on one fixed ordinary neighborhood, with harmonic weak smoothness, positivity and scalar compatibility proved.
detailedSummary: A countable extraction argument handles extended-real limits without replacing a general net silently. Finite normalization separates the branches at a singular rigid point. For a finite common target value, small upward shifts align approximant values; for a minus-infinity value, regularized maxima with a common level align them. Compact domination guarantees decrease on one fixed compact normalization neighborhood. Local constancy at rigid points gives actual constant neighborhoods downstairs. The result permits discontinuous targets, poles and identically minus-infinity branches, but remains a one-dimensional sufficient theorem under the stated field, reducedness and boundary assumptions.
text:
Draft theorem. Let K be complete, perfect and nontrivially valued, with a countable dense subset. Let C be a reduced Hausdorff good strictly K-analytic curve with empty analytic boundary. For every ordinary open D in C, every arbitrary classical psh u:D→R union {-infinity}, and every x in D, there is one fixed ordinary open neighborhood V of x and finite weakly smooth classical psh functions v_j on V decreasing pointwise to u. Their strong curvature currents are positive. The same sequence pulls back with these properties after every analytic extension. For finite continuous u, convergence is locally uniform.

The following arguments establish the new applications of the premises audited in n1.

Countable extraction. Suppose a_i is a directed decreasing net of finite continuous functions on a second-countable space Z, with infimum a, possibly minus infinity. For each rational q, the open sets {a_i<q} cover {a<q}. Every open subspace of a second-countable space is Lindelof, so countably many indices suffice for each q. Enumerate all these indices and successively choose directed upper bounds i_j. Then a_{i_j} decreases to a: for each z every rational q>a(z) eventually bounds its selected values, and if a(z)=-infinity every rational does. This extracts indices sufficient by values; it does not claim countable cofinality of the original index set.

The field assumption supplies this topology locally. A strict affinoid algebra is a Banach quotient of a Tate algebra. Polynomials with coefficients from a countable dense subfield are dense. A norm-dense sequence b_n supplies countably many evaluations generating the spectrum topology, since ||b(x)|-|c(x)||≤|b-c|(x)≤||b-c|| uniformly. They separate points and embed the compact spectrum in a countable product of bounded real intervals. Thus its spectrum and ordinary open subsets are second countable.

Compact domination. If continuous a_i decrease to a, A is compact, and continuous finite b satisfies b>a on A, then some a_i<b throughout A. The open sets {a_i<b} cover A; use a finite subcover and one directed upper bound. Additional finite index or point-value requirements can be imposed simultaneously. No continuity of a and no Dini theorem are needed.

Regularized maximum. Choose an even nonnegative smooth probability density rho supported in (-1,1). Set theta_delta(t)=integral |t+delta s|rho(s)ds and M_delta(a,b)=(a+b+theta_delta(a-b))/2. Convolution makes theta smooth and convex, with derivative in [-1,1]. Jensen and the triangle inequality give max(a,b)≤M_delta(a,b)≤max(a,b)+delta/2. It equals max when |a-b|≥delta, and is convex and nondecreasing in each variable.

Classical positivity of such compositions is proved, rather than inferred from smoothness. For finite continuous classical psh g_i and a smooth convex coordinatewise nondecreasing F, supporting affine functions of F have nonnegative coefficients. Finite maxima of their evaluations on the g_i are classical psh by GR 4.2. Their directed net converges pointwise to the continuous composition, so GR 6.5 proves its classical positivity. The same argument applies to a convex nondecreasing function of log|P| that is constant on a negative half-line; the constant supporting line handles zeros.

The GJR construction has the specific local smoothness needed here. After a finite Galois extension, an individual lisse target is represented on a finite skeleton. At a curvature vertex with outgoing slopes s_e and positive weights w_e, let mu=sum w_e s_e>0. Replacing every slope by s_e-mu/(sum w_e) gives a harmonic star function G, with the same vertex value and strictly below the target F off that vertex. A sufficiently small M_delta(G+epsilon,F), delta<epsilon, equals G+epsilon near the vertex and F near the outer ends. The equalities hold on ordinary neighborhoods and permit ordinary gluing. Arbitrary real subdivisions are not identified with strict formal-model skeletons.

The resulting functions are harmonic on the unchanged regions and near the curvature vertices. GJR 15.7 and 7.5 represent each real harmonic piece as a smooth affine function of finitely many integer harmonic coordinates. On each intervening annulus the function is a smooth convex Phi(t) of an invertible logarithmic coordinate. These are exactly harmonic-tropicalization weakly smooth descriptions. Finite Galois translates may be averaged to make the construction invariant, preserving positivity, approximation bounds and decreasing order; GJR 14.2 descends the resulting functions. Harmonic pieces and convex annular pieces are subharmonic, and ordinary sheafiness together with GR 3.4.1 and 4.1.2 gives classical positivity. Identically minus-infinity components have approximants -j.

The curvature formulas are zero on harmonic pieces and Phi''(t)d't wedge d''t on annular pieces, with Phi''≥0. Regularized maxima and subsequent convex compositions have positive semidefinite Hessians in these harmonic coordinates. Integer harmonic coordinates remain integer harmonic under every analytic morphism and scalar extension, by GJR 7.6. Thus these curvature formulas pull back and remain positive. A positive semidefinite Hessian is a sum of nonnegative rank-one forms ell wedge J ell. Against positive compactly supported tests of degree (d-1,d-1), the relevant Lagerberg cones coincide by CD 1.2.10. On a common harmonic chart the resulting top-degree form is nonnegative, and the tropical integration weights are nonnegative. Stokes gives <d'd''[g],eta>=integral d'd''g wedge eta≥0 on Hausdorff boundaryless pure-dimensional spaces. If the description is obtained after a finite Galois extension, GJR 14.5 gives equality of these integrals, without a degree factor. This proves positive strong currents and therefore positive CLD currents. It is a construction-specific positivity proof, not a general comparison of classical and current positivity for every weakly smooth function.

After any analytic extension L/K the coordinates pull back. Compositing an auxiliary finite Galois field with L gives a finite Galois extension of L, so the same integration argument proves positivity there. Classical positivity independently follows from GR 4.2(5). One constructed sequence is pulled back; a new extraction over L is unnecessary.

Proof at a nonsingular point. Normalization is an isomorphism there and is rig-smooth because K is perfect. Apply GJR 15.11 on a relatively compact ordinary smooth neighborhood, treating an identically minus-infinity component by constants, and use the countable extraction just proved.

Proof at a singular point. It is rigid. GR 3.9 allows shrinking to U with no other singularity, whose finite normalization is a disjoint union of finitely many connected smooth branches U_i, each with exactly one point x_i over x and an isomorphism away from those points. Choose the U_i relatively compact in slightly larger smooth neighborhoods inside a normalized strict affinoid neighborhood. They are second countable. Choose a compact strict affinoid neighborhood Y⊂U of x and put V=ordinary interior of Y and A_i=nu^{-1}(Y)∩U_i. Each A_i is compact. Write u_i=u∘nu and a=u(x)=u_i(x_i).

On each branch, GJR and countable extraction provide finite weakly smooth classical psh sequences s_{i,j} decreasing to u_i, with the curvature descriptions above. Use s_{i,j}=-j for an identically minus-infinity branch.

A weakly smooth function on a curve is locally constant at a rigid point. Its local preform uses finitely many integer harmonic coordinates, each strict PL. The proof of GR 3.9(6) records that at a rigid point a strict affinoid G-cover has a member containing an ordinary neighborhood and that invertible analytic absolute values are locally constant there. Hence each coordinate, and its smooth composition, is locally constant. We only need this assertion on the smooth normalization branches.

Let epsilon_0=1 and epsilon_j=8^{-j}. Upper semicontinuity bounds u_i above on the compact branch closures; choose a common constant h_{i,0}=H≥u_i+1. Inductively construct h_{i,j}≥u_i+epsilon_j, decreasing on A_i and taking the same value at all x_i.

If a is finite, choose late terms g_i of the branch sequences with g_i≤s_{i,j}, g_i<h_{i,j-1}-4epsilon_j on A_i, and a≤b_i=g_i(x_i)<a+epsilon_j. Compact domination applies because 4epsilon_j<epsilon_{j-1}; the point-value requirement follows from convergence. Put b=max_i b_i and h_{i,j}=g_i+(b-b_i)+epsilon_j. The upward shifts lie in [0,epsilon_j), and all node values equal b+epsilon_j. Moreover,
  u_i+epsilon_j≤h_{i,j}≤s_{i,j}+2epsilon_j,
  h_{i,j}<h_{i,j-1}-2epsilon_j on A_i.
These bounds prove decrease and convergence, including any other minus-infinity values. Constant shifts preserve all smoothness and positivity assertions.

If a=-infinity, choose c_j≤-j with c_j<min_A h_{j-1}-4epsilon_j. Choose late g_i≤s_{i,j} satisfying g_i<h_{i,j-1}-4epsilon_j on A_i and g_i(x_i)<c_j-epsilon_j. Set h_{i,j}=M_{epsilon_j}(g_i,c_j)+epsilon_j. It equals c_j+epsilon_j on an ordinary neighborhood of every x_i. The maximum bounds give
  u_i+epsilon_j≤h_{i,j}≤max(s_{i,j},c_j)+3epsilon_j/2,
  h_{i,j}<h_{i,j-1}-5epsilon_j/2 on A_i.
Since c_j→-infinity, these prove pointwise convergence on every branch, including identically minus-infinity branches. The convex-composition argument and curvature formulas prove classical positivity and positive strong currents.

Descent and ordinary overlaps. The h_{i,j} have a common constant value on neighborhoods of all x_i. Away from x use the normalization isomorphism. Near x, finiteness makes normalization closed and a quotient: remove the image of the closed complement of these neighborhoods to obtain an ordinary neighborhood downstairs where the descended function is constant. Thus the functions v_j on the fixed V are finite continuous and weakly smooth on actual ordinary neighborhoods, with compatible overlaps. GR finite surjective descent proves their classical positivity. Curvature is zero near the singularity and positive by the displayed formulas elsewhere. Decrease holds on the fixed compact normalization preimage, hence on the fixed V; the pointwise bounds give limit u. Scalar pullbacks have the properties already proved. For a finite continuous target, Dini on compact subsets gives local uniform convergence; no such convergence is claimed for arbitrary singular targets.

This includes unibranch cusps and nodal multibranch curves. It does not assert general weak-smooth descent along arbitrary finite morphisms, or a theorem over nonperfect fields. It is a draft mathematical proof, not a consequence of successful execution. The complete argument is retained in P02.3-argument.md, Sections 2–3, and P02.3-paper.tex. Rerun the presentation with python3 make_paper.py and python3 build_paper.py.

summary: Draft noninvariant higher-dimensional sector: all arbitrary classical psh functions on saturated proper connected-fibre domains with local sections over the curves of n2 descend and regularize on one fixed saturated ordinary neighborhood. Singular fibres are allowed. Nonsaturated affine germs remain outside the result.
detailedSummary: Proper connected fibres force extended-real classical psh functions to be constant by the maximum principle over completed residue fields. Local analytic sections make their descended base functions classical psh. Pulling back n2 gives weakly smooth positive decreasing sequences and compatibility with all analytic scalar extensions. Products with projective space or connected nodal projective curves give actual higher-dimensional examples without torus invariance. The domain quantifier is essential: this covers every function on each saturated domain, but not every sheaf germ on arbitrary smaller opens.
text:
Draft theorem. Let K and C satisfy n2. Let f:X→C be proper and surjective, with nonempty geometrically connected analytic fibres and analytic sections on an ordinary open cover of C. Assume X is Hausdorff, good, strictly analytic and pure of dimension d≥2. For every ordinary open D⊂C and every arbitrary classical psh u on the saturated domain f^{-1}(D), each x has one fixed ordinary neighborhood f^{-1}(V), f(x)∈V⊂D, carrying finite weakly smooth classical psh functions w_j with positive strong curvature currents and w_j decreasing pointwise to u. For finite continuous u the convergence is locally uniform. Every analytic scalar extension pulls back the same sequence with these properties. Neither normality nor smoothness of the fibres is required.

Proof of fibre constancy. For c∈D pass to the completed residue field H(c). GR scalar stability and pullback make the restriction of u to X_c classically psh. The proper connected fibre is compact and has empty analytic boundary. If u is not identically minus infinity there, upper semicontinuity gives a finite attained maximum M. Its maximum set is nonempty and closed; GR Theorem 6.1 makes it open because every fibre point is an analytic interior point. Connectedness makes it the whole fibre. If the restriction is identically minus infinity, it is already constant. This proves constancy on every fibre, including those over nonrigid base points; no density argument is used.

There is therefore a unique a:D→R union {-infinity} with u=a∘f. On each ordinary open possessing a section s, a=u∘s is upper semicontinuous and classically psh by GR pullback. These definitions agree on overlaps by fibre constancy. Ordinary sheafiness gives a classical psh base function a. Apply n2 at f(x), on a fixed V, and define w_j=v_j∘f.

The requested harmonic smoothness is explicit. A local harmonic preform (h,alpha) for v_j pulls back to (h∘f,alpha). GJR 7.6 preserves the integer harmonic coordinates. Equality on overlapping charts is pulled back through the joint chart (h,h'), as in GJR Definition 10.3 and Proposition 10.9. The zero-curvature and positive-Hessian descriptions established in n2 pull back; over the constant neighborhood of a singular base point the curvature is zero. The integration argument in n2 proves positive strong currents. Properness gives empty relative boundary, and the boundaryless base gives empty absolute boundary for X and f^{-1}(V), so the current argument has no boundary residues.

For any analytic extension L/K, let p:X_L→X. On the fixed ordinary domain p^{-1}(f^{-1}(V))=f_L^{-1}(V_L), the sequence is w_j∘p. At each z its values decrease to u(p(z)). Harmonic coordinate pullback, the scalar positivity proof in n2 and GR scalar stability prove the other assertions. This is extension of one base-field sequence, not descent of arbitrarily chosen extension-field approximants. If u is finite continuous, its restriction through local sections makes a finite continuous; compact images under f transfer the local uniform convergence of v_j to w_j.

Concrete examples are F^an×C with F geometrically connected and proper, possessing a K-point, and with the displayed product pure-dimensional. A point of F supplies a section. F=P^m gives dimension m+1. A geometrically connected reduced nodal projective curve F gives a singular surface when C is a curve. For C=A1^an, log|T-a| pulled back from the base, a≠0, gives a classical target with a genuine pole; on a torus open it is generally not maximal-compact-torus invariant. The theorem assumes no torus invariance of any target.

The saturated-domain restriction is indispensable to this proof. On an affine chart of P^m×C, log|Z_1| is classical psh and varies along the affine fibres. Those fibres are not the compact proper fibres used above. Consequently this result cannot be advertised as regularization of all sheaf germs on the product or as a characterization of the original higher-dimensional local property.

The mathematical proof and limitation are retained in P02.3-argument.md, Section 4, and standalone P02.3-paper.tex. Rerun python3 make_paper.py and python3 build_paper.py. Successful builds do not verify fibre constancy, descent or the new proof.

summary: Sharp boundary-spike family: the closed-disc function equal to 1 at the Gauss point and 0 elsewhere is classically psh. Uncountable residue fields prohibit any continuous approximating sequence near that boundary point; countable residue fields admit an explicit decreasing weakly smooth psh sequence. Products give higher-dimensional sequential failures. Nets and the general characterization remain unresolved.
detailedSummary: Polynomial reductions show that every neighborhood of the Gauss point contains rational points in all but finitely many residue classes, producing an obstruction to any pointwise continuous sequence when the residue field is uncountable. With countable residue field, lifted irreducible residue polynomials and a smooth concave cutoff construct an explicit decreasing sequence on the whole closed disc. Coprimality ensures at most one active summand. Convex logarithmic profiles prove harmonic weak smoothness, classical positivity and positive curvature on the analytic interior. Pullbacks converge to the pullback function, not a newly defined single-point spike. The residue-countability threshold is exact for this particular target, not a characterization for all targets or all spaces.
text:
Draft boundary theorem. Let K be any complete nontrivially valued field, E=M(K<T>) the strict closed unit disc, and xi its radius-one Gauss point. Define b(xi)=1 and b(z)=0 otherwise. Then b is an upper semicontinuous classical psh function. If the residue field is uncountable, b is not the pointwise limit of any sequence of finite continuous functions on any ordinary neighborhood of xi, even without monotonicity. If the residue field is countable, the explicit construction below gives finite weakly smooth classical psh functions decreasing to b on the whole fixed E, with positive curvature on its analytic interior.

Classical membership. The actual analytic boundary of E is {xi}. For 0<a≤1, {b<a}=E\{xi} is open, so b is upper semicontinuous. It is constant zero on Int(E). GR Proposition 3.5(3) makes it subharmonic on E, and GR 4.1.2 makes it classically psh, including the required tests after every analytic extension. This is an analytic-boundary function, not an interior spike on a boundaryless space.

Neighborhood lemma. Every ordinary neighborhood N of xi contains rational points from all but finitely many residue classes. Polynomial evaluations generate the spectrum topology because polynomials are uniformly dense in the Tate algebra. Choose a basic neighborhood given by finitely many polynomial absolute-value conditions. Normalize each nonzero polynomial by a coefficient of maximum absolute value; its reduction is a nonzero residue polynomial. It has only finitely many roots in the residue field. For a lift a∈K° of a residue class avoiding these roots, every selected polynomial has precisely its Gauss absolute value at a. Thus a lies in N.

Uncountable-residue obstruction. Suppose continuous q_j on N converge pointwise to b. Discard finitely many terms so q_j(xi)>3/4. Each {q_j>3/4}∩N is a neighborhood of xi and excludes rational points from only finitely many residue classes. An uncountable residue field has a class outside the countable union of these exceptions. Choose a lift a of that class. Then q_j(a)>3/4 for every remaining j, contradicting b(a)=0. Since weakly smooth functions are continuous, this excludes the requested sequential regularization. It does not exclude decreasing nets.

Countable-residue construction. Enumerate the monic irreducible polynomials of the residue field as p_1,p_2,... and choose monic coefficientwise lifts P_i∈K°[T], each of Gauss norm one. Let sigma be a smooth nonnegative probability density supported in (0,1), symmetric about 1/2, and set
  eta(t)=2 integral from t to 1 of sigma(s) ds,
  psi(t)=integral from 0 to t of eta(s) ds,
with sigma zero outside (0,1). Then eta is smooth, nonnegative and nonincreasing, equals 2 for t≤0 and 0 for t≥1. Thus psi is smooth, increasing and concave, with psi(0)=0 and psi(t)=1 for t≥1; the latter follows from 2 integral_0^1 s sigma(s)ds=1.

Define
  v_j(z)=1-sum_{i=1}^j psi(j[-log|P_i(z)|]),
with a summand defined to be 1 at a zero of P_i. This convention agrees on a whole neighborhood of each zero, because psi is constant for arguments at least 1.

At most one |P_i(z)| is less than one. Otherwise two coprime reductions admit a Bezout identity whose lift would express 1 as terms of absolute value strictly less than one plus an error polynomial of Gauss norm strictly less than one, contradicting the ultrametric inequality. Therefore 0≤v_j≤1. Existing summands increase with j and new summands are nonnegative, so v_{j+1}≤v_j.

If all |P_i(z)|=1, every polynomial has its Gauss norm at z. To see this, normalize the polynomial, factor its reduction into the p_i, and compare it with the corresponding product of lifts. Their difference has Gauss norm less than one. Consequently z=xi by equality of polynomial seminorms. Every other z has exactly one i with |P_i(z)|<1; its summand is eventually exactly 1. Hence v_j(z)→0 away from xi and v_j(xi)=1 throughout.

Smoothness and positivity. Write H_j(s)=1-psi(-js). It is smooth, convex and nondecreasing on R, and zero for s≤-1/j. Each H_j(log|P_i|) is locally constant near the zero set and elsewhere a smooth function of an invertible analytic logarithm. It is therefore weakly smooth through an actual smooth harmonic tropicalization; ordinary CLD smoothness here follows from the explicit coordinates, not from a weak-smooth label. Classical positivity follows from the supporting-line argument in n2, including the constant supporting line at zeros. Since
  v_j=sum_{i=1}^j H_j(log|P_i|)-(j-1),
the cone and constant properties prove classical positivity. Its local curvature is the sum of
  H_j''(log|P_i|) d'log|P_i| wedge d''log|P_i|,
with nonnegative coefficients. The integration argument in n2 gives positive strong and CLD currents on Int(E). No boundary-free integration-by-parts assertion is made on the entire closed disc.

All formulas pull back after every analytic extension, remain weakly smooth and classically psh, remain decreasing, and converge to b∘p. That pullback can equal 1 at more than one extension-field point; it is not replaced by a new single-point Gauss spike.

Higher-dimensional failure. For m≥1 take X=E×P^{m,an} and u=b∘pr_E. This is classical psh on a separated good strict pure-dimensional space of dimension m+1. Fix a K-rational projective point p and x=(xi,p). The analytic section s(z)=(z,p) pulls any alleged sequence on an ordinary neighborhood of x back to a continuous sequence on an ordinary neighborhood of xi, already proved impossible when the residue field is uncountable. Projection is proper with no relative boundary; boundary composition over the locally separated disc gives partial X=pr_E^{-1}({xi}). Thus x is an actual analytic boundary point. A concrete field is C((t)) with its complete nontrivial t-adic valuation. For an extension of this uncountable-residue example, the same obstruction uses the uncountable image of the original residue field. The countable-residue construction proves that countability is the exact threshold for this particular boundary-spike target; it is not a sufficient condition for all disc targets.

Remaining original obligations. The positive higher-dimensional result n3 concerns saturated domains, not all nonsaturated affine sheaf germs. The full boundaryless higher-dimensional arbitrary-class problem, a sharp necessary-and-sufficient geometric characterization, general singularity and scalar-descent ranges, nonperfect fields, general nonseparable-field targets, nonseparated spaces and other analytic boundary configurations remain unresolved here. The obstruction is sequential and does not establish failure for nets. No known curve or invariant toric endpoint is identified with the original characterization.

The full proof and remaining obligations are retained in P02.3-argument.md, Sections 5–6, and P02.3-paper.tex. status.json has exactly id,status,exact_result,proof_file,concrete_gaps and marks P02.3 partial. python3 audit_artifacts.py reported all ten artifact checks true. Both final TeX passes returned zero and produced a 10-page PDF, with no diagnostics on the second pass. These are execution observations; the new proofs remain unverified drafts. Rerun python3 collect_sources.py; python3 make_paper.py; python3 build_paper.py; python3 audit_artifacts.py. The entire original target and its sharp general range have not been solved.
